passages.provision_quote: A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enrolled text of SB 101 sets the compelling-interest/least-restrictive-means standard that matches rung 4's faith-based exemption clause.
Clere is listed among the Nay votes on final House passage of SB 101.

rows.reasoning: SB 101 (2015) sets a compelling-interest/least-restrictive-means standard for religious exemptions, matching rung 4's clause 'allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs' and excluded from rung 5 by the same compelling-interest test. Clere voted Nay on final passage, which rules out support for that broad exemption standard but does not, by itself, establish which of rungs 1 through 3 he holds, so the vote is direction-only.
